summary: New-hire provisioning: OOBE cycle after imaging due to duplicate Azure AD device object
description:
Issue summary: New employee's laptop repeatedly returned to Windows OOBE screen after the standard company image was applied and device was Auto-joined to Azure AD. Impact: blocked new hire onboarding for two business days; access to company resources delayed. Environment: corporate image (Win11-Redwood-2026-v3), Intune autopilot-like provisioning flow, Azure AD tenancy (redwood-prod), device model: Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen3.

Root observation: Imaging completed locally, but on first boot the machine went through OOBE, attempted to join Azure AD, failed with a 0x801c0006-ish registration error, and then restarted back to OOBE. This loop repeated on subsequent attempts. Removing the device object from Azure AD allowed a single successful join and normal provisioning.

Why this matters: This appears to be a race/duplication condition introduced when reseller/hardware-import created a stale device object before IT imaging workflow attempted to register the device. If it recurs at scale it will impact new-hire ramp time and increase manual overhead for helpdesk.
impact: One new hire unable to complete provisioning for ~18 hours; 2 other recently imaged devices showed intermittent registration failures but recovered after manual clean-up.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Acquire device with vendor-provisioned serial that has existing device object in Azure AD (vendor pre-registration).
2) Apply corporate image Win11-Redwood-2026-v3 via provisioning workstation (network boot + SCCM task sequence).
3) Allow device to boot to OOBE and attempt Azure AD Join using local autopilot/Intune flow.
4) Observe Azure AD registration failure and automatic OOBE restart, repeat loop.
5) Remove stale device object from Azure AD portal (Devices > All devices > Delete), reboot device and proceed through OOBE.
logs: AAD registration error (from Event Viewer): AADSTS9002313 - Another device with same certificate exists.
Provisioning logs: SCCM/TaskSequence finished successfully (0x0) prior to OOBE loop.
AzureAD Join log snippet (dsregcmd /status): DeviceId present but registrationState=Failed; errorCode=0x801c0006.
Intune enrollment log: HTTP 409 response when posting device enrollment record (conflict: existing device).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: image/build issue or corrupted offline profile. Reimaged twice with same result -> rules out image payload corruption.

Observed correlation between serial numbers recently imported by procurement's vendor CSV and failures. Cross-checked 3 failing serials; each had pre-existing device entries in Azure AD with 'Registered' state and vendor user tag.

Test case: Created a fresh temporary device object, attempted registration -> succeeded. Deleted vendor-created device object, re-registered original device -> succeeded. Suggests duplicate-object conflict in Azure AD device registration.
Checked automation: procurement vendor imports run nightly and sometimes create device objects without 'managedBy'. No existing dedupe check in import script.
SRE note: No backend service outages during incident window; rates low so not quota-related.
comments: 2026-03-05 10:12 - Avery Collins: Reported by new-hire laptop owner via #internal-helpdesk. Confirmed OOBE loop; attached dsregcmd logs. Escalated to imaging team.

2026-03-05 13:30 - Maya Hernandez (Assignee): Reimaged device twice locally, reproduced OOBE loop. Cleared vendor device object in AAD as a test; device joined successfully and finished autopilot. Marking as likely duplicate-device issue. Will coordinate with procurement.

2026-03-06 09:05 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Checked AAD audit logs for device creation times. Found vendor import job creating device entries at 02:15 UTC nightly. 3 of 12 recent failures link to those timestamps.

2026-03-07 15:22 - Procurement (Priya Kapoor): We pulled vendor import script and found no dedupe step. Opened PR to add serial-based deduplication and to tag vendor-created entries with 'vendor-provisioned' attribute. See PR referenced above.

2026-03-08 11:40 - Maya Hernandez: Deployed temporary remediation runbook to helpdesk: check AAD for pre-existing device objects and delete before imaging, or add a pre-image cleanup step to SCCM task sequence. Also added steps to the device-registration-playbook.
2026-03-09 08:55 - Avery Collins: New-hire confirmed laptop works and has access to Slack, VPN, and internal apps. Closing ticket with follow-up action owned by procurement.
2026-03-09 09:10 - Maya Hernandez: Adding follow-up tasks to procurement backlog and filing INT-9974 to implement automated pre-imaging check.
resolution: Root cause: duplicate/stale device objects created by vendor import automation caused Azure AD registration conflicts during OOBE, triggering a registration failure loop. Fixes: (1) Immediate: helpdesk runbook added to remove stale device objects before imaging; (2) Medium-term: procurement import script updated with serial-number deduplication and vendor tag (PR #42); (3) Long-term: add an automated pre-imaging AAD check in SCCM task sequence (follow-up ticket INT-9974).
follow_up_actions: INT-9974 - Implement pre-imaging AAD device existence check in SCCM task sequence (owner: Imaging team)
Procurement PR #42 - Add dedupe logic and vendor tagging to import script (owner: Procurement/Platform)
Update Confluence runbook: device-registration-playbook to include troubleshooting checklist for OOBE loops (owner: IT Ops)
Monitor for repeat failures for 30 days and report metrics weekly to ops-review
